12681-us-and-the-bottle-man.creator: Unknown
12681-us-and-the-bottle-man.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. we'd never heard from any of them, although one reason for that was that we never put our address on them. We decided we would this time, because Jerry had just been reading about a fisherman in Newfoundland picking up a message that somebody had chucked from a yacht in the Gulf of Mexico months and months before.

arxiv-2102-04394.title: Learning with Density Matrices and Random Features
arxiv-2102-04394.creator: Fabio A. González, Alejandro Gallego, Santiago Toledo-Cortés, Vladimir Vargas-Calderón
arxiv-2102-04394.description: Abstract 2021 A density matrix describes the statistical state of a quantum system. It is a powerful formalism to represent both the quantum and classical uncertainty of quantum systems and to express different statistical operations such as measurement, system combination and expectations as linear algebra operations.

arxiv-2209-08318.title: Hausdorff dimension of sets with restricted, slowly growing partial quotients in semi-regular continued fractions Thanks: Keywords : continued fractions; Hausdorff dimension; iterated function system (IFS)
arxiv-2209-08318.creator: Yuto Nakajima and Hiroki Takahasi
arxiv-2209-08318.description: Abstract . We determine the Hausdorff dimension of sets of irrationals in ( 0 , 1 ) (0,1) whose partial quotients in semi-regular continued fractions obey certain restrictions and growth conditions. This result substantially generalizes that of the second author [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 151 (2023), 3645–3653] and the solution of Hirst’s conjecture [B.-W. Wang and J. Wu, Bull.

arxiv-2210-08860.title: Automatic Analysis of Human Body Representations in Western Art
arxiv-2210-08860.creator: Shu Zhao, Almıla Akdağ Salah, Albert Ali Salah
arxiv-2210-08860.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shu Zhao, Almıla Akdağ Salah, Albert Ali Salah. The way the human body is depicted in classical and modern paintings is relevant for art historical analyses. Each artist has certain themes and concerns, resulting in different poses being used more heavily than others. In this paper, we propose a computer vision pipeline to analyse human pose and representations in paintings, which can be used for specific artists or periods.

arxiv-2409-00547.title: Data Augmentation for Image Classification using Generative AI
arxiv-2409-00547.creator: Fazle Rahat, M Shifat Hossain, Md Rubel Ahmed, Sumit Kumar Jha, Rickard Ewetz
arxiv-2409-00547.description: Abstract Scaling laws dictate that the performance of AI models is proportional to the amount of available data. Data augmentation is a promising solution to expanding the dataset size. Traditional approaches focused on augmentation using rotation, translation, and resizing. Recent approaches use generative AI models to improve dataset diversity.

arxiv-2412-07623.title: Direct Fidelity Estimation for Generic Quantum States
arxiv-2412-07623.creator: Christopher Vairogs, Bin Yan
arxiv-2412-07623.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Christopher Vairogs, Bin Yan. Verifying the proper preparation of quantum states is essential in modern quantum information science. Various protocols have been developed to estimate the fidelity of quantum states produced by different parties. Direct fidelity estimation is a leading approach, as it typically requires a number of measurements that scale linearly with the Hilbert space dimension, making it far more efficient than full state tomography.

arxiv-2505-06540.title: Differential inclusion systems with fractional competing operator and multivalued fractional convection term
arxiv-2505-06540.creator: Jinxia Cen, Salvatore A. Marano, Shengda Zeng
arxiv-2505-06540.description: Abstract In this work, the existence of solutions (in a suitable sense) to a family of inclusion systems involving fractional, possibly competing, elliptic operators, fractional convection, and homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions is established. The technical approach exploits Galerkin’s method and a surjective results for multifunctions in finite dimensional spaces as well as approximating techniques.

arxiv-2510-07354.title: Quantum Algorithm for Binary Vector Encoding and Retrieval Utilizing the Permutation Trick
arxiv-2510-07354.creator: Andreas Wichert
arxiv-2510-07354.description: Abstract We present a novel quantum storage algorithm for k k binary vectors of dimension m m into a superposition of a m m -qubit quantum state based on a permutation technique. We compare this algorithm to the storage algorithm proposed by Ventura and Martinez.

arxiv-2601-21889.title: Orbital decomposition of the nuclear regions in the early-type galaxy FCC 47: Unveiling the nuclear cluster origin
arxiv-2601-21889.creator: J. Lamprecht, A. Feldmeier-Krause, M. Lyubenova, K. Fahrion, S. Thater, P. Jethwa, S. Reiter, J. Falcón-Barroso, T. I. Maindl, G. Santucci, I. Breda
arxiv-2601-21889.description: Abstract Context. Nuclear star clusters (NSCs) are among the densest stellar systems in the Universe and often coexist with supermassive black holes (SMBHs) at galaxy centres. While SMBH formation histories are essentially lost, NSCs preserve evolutionary imprints through their stellar populations and stellar kinematics, reflecting the cumulative effects of mergers, accretion, and internal dynamical evolution. Aims.

pmc-11362964.title: Research Status of Lignin-Based Polyurethane and Its Application in Flexible Electronics
pmc-11362964.creator: Jingbo Hu, Mengmeng Huang, Xing Zhou, Rubai Luo, Lu Li, Xiaoning Li
pmc-11362964.description: Polyurethanes (PU) have drawn great attention due to their excellent mechanical properties and self-healing and recyclable abilities. Lignin is a natural and renewable raw material in nature, composed of a large number of hydroxyl groups, and has a great potential to replace petroleum polyols in PU synthesis.

pmc-11450573.title: Genetic Architectures of Medical Images Revealed by Registration of Multiple Modalities
pmc-11450573.creator: Sam Freesun Friedman, Gemma Elyse Moran, Marianne Rakic, Anthony Phillipakis
pmc-11450573.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The advent of biobanks with vast quantities of medical imaging and paired genetic measurements creates huge opportunities for a new generation of genotype–phenotype association studies. However, disentangling biological signals from the many sources of bias and artifacts remains difficult. Using diverse medical images and time-series (ie, magnetic resonance imagings [MRIs], electrocardiograms [ECGs], and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometries [DXAs]), we show how registration, both spatial and temporal, guided by domain knowledge or learned de novo, helps uncover biological information.

pmc-11490708.title: -AI-assisted diagnostic potential of CT in bone oncology and its impact on clinical decision-making for intensive care
pmc-11490708.creator: Wei Hua, Bing Xu, Xianwen Zhang, Tingting Chen
pmc-11490708.description: Highlights•AI-assisted diagnostic potential of CT for bone cancer and its impact on patient care.•Conducted retrospective analysis of 50 patients with bone cancer by SPECT and histopathology.•Timely CT examination is crucial in achieving accurate staging of bone tumors.•Specific consolidation patterns and extent of lesion spread were predictive of risks necessitating ICU intervention.

pmc-11561479.title: Association of Lipoprotein(a) With Severe Degenerative Aortic Valve Stenosis
pmc-11561479.creator: Ah-Ram Kim, Jung-Min Ahn, Do-Yoon Kang, Tae Joon Jun, Byung Joo Sun, Ho Jin Kim, Joon Bum Kim, Dae-Hee Kim, Duk-Woo Park, Young-Hak Kim, Ki Hoon Han, Seung-Jung Park
pmc-11561479.description: BackgroundLipoprotein(a) (Lp[a]) is associated with the development of aortic valve calcification.ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to evaluate the association between the serum level of Lp(a) and the development of severe degenerative aortic stenosis (AS) and subsequent aortic valve replacement (AVR).

pmc-11653880.title: Integrative Proteomics and Phosphoproteomics Profiling of Symptomatic Accessory Navicular Bone Based on Tandem Mass Tag Technology
pmc-11653880.creator: Bin Liu, Ran Wei, Yuqing Wang, Zishen Cheng, Liangliang Jiang, Xiaopeng Pu, Yaxing Zhang, Yantao Wang, Qiangjun Kang
pmc-11653880.description: BackgroundThe accessory navicular bone (ANB) is a common accessory bone in the foot. Certain ANBs significantly impair patients’ feet normal walking function. Foot injury is associated with ANB after athletic training. However, the molecular mechanism of foot injury with ANB after athletic training remains unclear.

pmc-11709530.title: Defining the Problem History Heterogeneity in Patients with Alzheimer’s Disease: A Data‐Driven Approach
pmc-11709530.creator: Clayton Mansel, Ryan A Townley, Robyn A Honea, Mihaela E Sardiu, Olivia J Veatch
pmc-11709530.description: BackgroundThe medical and social history of patients with Alzheimer’s Disease is heterogeneous with many interacting genetic and environmental factors contributing to an individual’s risk. Moreover, a maternal family history (mFH) is a key risk factor for AD—raising the risk for disease onset by as much as nine times.

pmc-12641264.title: Metabolite-responsive scaffold RNAs for dynamic CRISPR transcriptional regulation
pmc-12641264.creator: Anthony M Stohr, Helena Hansen, Blake Richards, Hayeon Park, Antonio G Goncalves, Ayushi Agrawal, Mark Blenner, Wilfred Chen
pmc-12641264.description: CRISPR activation is a powerful tool to upregulate a vast array of genes in many different contexts. However, there are few dynamic CRISPR transcriptional programs, which limit its usage in the creation of living biosensors, self-regulating microbial factories, or conditional therapeutics.

pmc-12843303.title: Biomechanical Investigation of Head Injuries Caused by Baseball Bat Strikes with Different Bat Sizes and Velocities: A Finite Element Simulation Study
pmc-12843303.creator: Han Zhang, Jin Yang, Luyi Guo, Jiani Sun, Shangxiao Li, Weiya Hao
pmc-12843303.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Objective: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) represents a significant clinical problem, with the biomechanical mechanisms of striking from different blunt instruments remaining unclear. This study aims to quantitatively evaluate TBI severity under blunt strikes and to assess the effects of strike velocity and blunt instrument size on biomechanical responses to provide a finite element approach for investigating injury mechanisms and informing clinical diagnosis.

pmc-13178321.title: Application value of biplane ultrasound combined with multimodal ultrasound elastography and ultra-micro angiography in stress urinary incontinence: a prospective clinical study
pmc-13178321.creator: Yu Hong, Dian Tao, Liuming Xiao, Zehong Zhou, Churuo Zhang, Muhan Su, Yanyan Zhu, Lingyu Xie, Shu’e Zeng, Rui Zhang, Hongwei Yang
pmc-13178321.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundStress urinary incontinence (SUI) is the most prevalent phenotype of female urinary incontinence. Conventional pelvic-floor ultrasound depends on a patient-performed Valsalva maneuver and therefore often fails to detect incipient or occult SUI. Transvaginal biplane ultrasound (TV-BPUS) combined with shear-wave elastography and ultra-micro angiography (UMA) can quantify urethral sphincter thickness, stiffness, and microperfusion at rest, allowing for subclinical alterations to be visualized.

pmc-13334590.title: EpCAM+ Extracellular Vesicle PD‐L1 Dynamics as a Predictive Biomarker of Immune Checkpoint Blockade Response
pmc-13334590.creator: Byeonggeol Mun, Jinyoung Kim, Chang Gon Kim, Seokhyeong Go, Mina Han, Yujin Ouck, Soojin Jang, Seong Uk Son, Gamin Kim, Wonrak Son, Eunjung Kim, Min Hee Hong, Ja Hyun Yeo, Eun‐Kyung Lim, Hye Ryun Kim, Seungjoo Haam
pmc-13334590.description: Programmed death‐ligand 1 (PD‐L1) blockade improves outcomes in patients with various malignancies; however, biomarkers for monitoring treatment responses are lacking. This study presents a surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS)‐based platform for the ultrasensitive detection of PD‐L1 on circulating epithelial cell adhesion molecule‐positive (EpCAM+) extracellular vesicles (EVs). The platform is validated using interferon‐gamma‐treated epithelial tumor cell line‐derived EVs.

pmc-13401223.title: Speech and Language Therapists’ Views and Experiences of Working With People With Wernicke's Aphasia: A Qualitative Interview Study
pmc-13401223.creator: Susanna Williams, Freyja Bell, Sarah Northcott, Suzanne Beeke
pmc-13401223.description: BackgroundWernicke's aphasia is a challenging communication disability to live with, characterised by fluent speech, impaired auditory comprehension and reduced self‐monitoring. There is little literature addressing functional therapy approaches. For example, there is limited evidence for communication partner training (CPT) for this client group, despite research on its effectiveness more generally.
